A. Balance Sheet
A.1 Assets
Fixed assets (Schedule 4) Rs. 199.20 crore
The composite cost of the Freehold Land and Leasehold Land are required to be made separately in the
Fixed Asset Schedule and Leasehold land should be amortized over the period of lease unless the lease is
in perpetuity.
However, BIS had not amortized/depreciated the Leasehold land in the Fixed Assets since acquiring
leasehold lands for Rs. 4.78 crore in 3 March, 1998 at NITS, Noida for a period of 90 years. In case of BIS
(HQ), RSBO, WRO, Jammu & Kashmir, NRO (Chandigarh), JBO, ERO Land-I and ERO-Land-2, no amortization
was required as period of lease has not been determined. There was less deduction of amortization/
depreciation of Rs. 1.22 crore (Rs. 47750000/90*23 years) for 23 years at NITS, Noida. This had resulted
B. General
in overstatement of fixed assets and understatement of Expenditure by Rs. 1.22 crore.
1. The Institute is accounting Pay and Allowances and Leave encashment on Cash basis which is in
contravention of accrual method of accounting as prescribed in Uniform Format of Accounts.
2. The discrepancies were noticed in the bank reconciliation statement as on 31 March, 2021. Cheques
issued but not encashed amounting to Rs. 2.07 crore should be written back and shown as liability in
the accounts. The amounts of Rs. 0.65 crore credited by Banks was not taken in accounts and entered
in the cash book after pursuing with the banks.
3. An amount of Rs. 27.03 lakh and Rs. 22.40 lakh remained unlinked as on 31 March, 2021 pertaining
to Canara Bank A/c No. 90841010000018 & Canara Bank 90842180024625 respectively. Moreover,
Rs. 47,664 also still remained unlinked as on 31 March, 2021 pertaining to Canara Bank A/c No.
C. Grants-in-aid
90841010000018 respectively. The same needs to be cleared before close of the financial year.
During 2021-21, BIS received Grants-in-aid of Rs. 1.00 crore for setting up of Hallmarking Centres and
for quality infrastructure for consumer protection from the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public
Distribution. It had Rs. 0.05 crore as interest income and unspent balance of Rs. 7.99 crore of the previous
year. Out of total available amount of Rs. 9.04 crore, a sum of Rs. 6.77 crore was utilized during the year
D. Management Letter
leaving a balance of Rs. 2.27 crore at the end of the year i.e on 31 March, 2021.
Deficiencies which have not been included in the Audit Report have been brought to the notice of the
Bureau of Indian Standards through a Management Letter issued separately for remedial/corrective action.
(v) Subject to our observations in the preceding paragraphs, we report that the Balance Sheet, Income
& Expenditure Account and Receipts & Payments Account dealt with by this report are in agreement
with the books of accounts.
(vi) In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanation given to us, the
said financial statements, read together with the Accounting Policies and Notes on Accounts, and
subject to the significant matters stated above and other matters mentioned in Annexure to this
Audit Report, give a true and fair view in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted
in India:
a. In so far as they relate to the Balance Sheet of the state of affairs of the Bureau of Indian
Standards as at 31 March, 2021; and
b. In so far as they relate to the Income and Expenditure Account of the surplus for the year ended
on that date.

(Keerti Tewari)

MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(Department of Consumer Affairs)
ORDER
New Delhi, the 28th April, 2026
S.O. 2117(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (3) of section 14 read with
sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 15, sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 16, section 17 and sub-section (3)
of section 25 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 (11 of 2016), the Central Government, is of the
opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do in the public interest, after consulting the Bureau of Indian
Standards, hereby makes the following order, further to amend the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold
Artefacts Order, 2020, namely:-
1. Short title and commencement. -(1) This order may be called the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold
Artefacts (Second Amendment) Order, 2026.
(2) It shall come into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

DELAY STATEMENT
Section 23 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 lays down that the
Central Government shall cause the Annual Report to be laid, as soon as may be,
after it is received, before each House of Parliament.
2. Rule 45 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules, 2018 stipulates that the
Bureau shall prepare its Annual Report and forward it to the Central Government
within nine months of the end of the financial year for being laid before each House
of Parliament. Accordingly, as per the provisions in the BIS Act and rules framed
thereunder, Bureau is required to submit its Annual Report to the Central
Government by 31 December each year for laying before each House of
st
Parliament.
3. However, Annual Report for the year 2018-19 could not be submitted to the
Central Government by 31 December, 2019. The chronology of finalization of
st
Annual Report and its submission to the Central Government is as under :-
(i) Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) submitted its Annual Accounts to
Controller and Auditor General of India (CAG) on 2ih June, 2019;
(ii) The Audit of Accounts of BIS for the year 2018-19 completed by CAG on
13.09.2019;
(iii) Draft Annual Report for 2018-19 was sent by BIS to this Department on
06,11.2019.
:to
.1
(iv) The Draft Audit Report was received from CAG by SIS on 18.11.2019 for
giving replies;
(v) SIS submitted its replies to the Draft Audit Report to CAG on 22.11.2019
(vi) The approval of the Hon'ble Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public
Distribution and President of the Governing Council of SIS was conveyed
on 12.12.2019.
(vii) The final Separate Audit Report (SAR) 2018-19 was received from the
office of Audit on 09.01.2020.
(viii) SIS submitted the final Annual Report to the Central Government on
29.01.2020 for laying in both the Houses of Parliament.
4. Hence, the delay in laying the Annual Report of SIS in both the Houses of
Parliament is mainly due to delay in receipt of final Audit Report from CAG.
******
LOKSABHA

clause_title: Preamble
text:
REVIEW OF BIS ANNUAL REPORT 2015-16
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) was set up on 01 April 1987 as a statutory body, taking
over the functions of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution (ISI). Its major activities
include formulation of Standards, product certification, hallmarking, management systems
certification, laboratory services and sales of Indian Standards and training services.
Besides, it is also engaged in consumer related and promotional activities.
BIS Act, 2016 has been notified by the Central Government on 22 March 2016 for general
information.
Major achievements of BIS during the year 2015-16, as reported in its Annual Report are
summarized below:
STANDARDIZATION
BIS is formulating need-based Indian standards in line with the National Priorities in a time-
bound manner. It also harmonizes National Standards with International Standards in order
to facilitate adoption of International Standards by all segments of industry and business.
A total of 264 Technical committee meetings were held during 2015-16 to consider draft
standards and related technical documents. It is the policy of BIS to formulate Indian
Standards on emerging technologies and to withdraw obsolete standards.
During the year, 609 standards (new 336 and revised 273) were formulated. The total number
of standards in force, as on 31 March 2016 was 18781.
PRODUCT CERTIFICATION
During the year, 3555 new licences were granted, which included 27 products covered for
the first time under the scheme. The total number of Indian Standards which have been
covered under BIS Certification Scheme are 941. The total number of operative licences as
on 31 March 2016 was 31347.
Surveillance and Licensees Meet
During the year, a total number of 11763 inspections and 6665 lot inspections were carried
out, in order to monitor the operation of licences. In addition about 22288 samples (including
samples procured from market) were drawn for independent testing. In order to acquire
feedback on the operation of the BIS Certification Marks Scheme, 49 review meetings with
the licensees were organized.
Foreign Manufactures Certification Scheme (FMCS)
BIS has been operating separate certification Foreign Manufacturers Certification scheme
(FMCS). Under this scheme, foreign manufacturers can seek certification from BIS for use
1
of BIS Standard Mark on their product(s). During 2015-16, 68 licences were issued under
FMCS, taking the total number of operative licences to 511 against 73 Indian Standards.
Compulsory Registration Scheme
The Compulsory Registration Scheme is being operated by BIS under the BIS Act, 1986 and
the Rules framed thereunder. The Department of Electronics and Information Technology
(DeitY) in consultation with BIS, notified "Electronics and Information Technology Goods
(Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012" on 3 Oct 2012 mandating
Compulsory Registration from BIS for 15 Electronics and IT products based on its safety
compliance to Indian Standards. A second Order was notified on 13 November 2014,
bringing 15 more electronics and IT products under the ambit of the Scheme. As on 31 March
2016, BIS has granted 4279 registrations to manufacturers in various countries.
LABORATORY SERVICES
In order to support the activities of the product certification marks scheme, BIS has
established eight laboratories in the country to cater to the testing of samples. The first BIS
Central laboratory was established at Sahibabad in 1962. Subsequently, four regional
laboratories, at Mohali, Kolkata, Mumbai and Chennai and three branch office laboratories
at Patna, Bangalore and Guwahati were established.
During the year, the BIS laboratories have tested 15815 samples of various products covered
under Certification. In addition, to support the Hallmarking Scheme of gold and silver
jewellery / artefacts, the Gold Referral Assaying Laboratory at Chennai has carried out and
issued 2559 test reports during the 2015-16.
Laboratory Recognition Scheme
BIS has established Laboratory Recognition Scheme (LRS) for recognition of outside
laboratories (OSLs). The services of such laboratories are utilized when it is economically
not viable to develop test facilities in BIS laboratories or when BIS laboratories do not have
the required capacity. As on 31 March 2016, the total number of BIS recognized outside
laboratories were 160, which include R&D organizations, technical institutions, Government
laboratories and private sector laboratories. Besides this, services of 47 Government
laboratories of specialized nature were also utilized for different products, as and when
required. To support the newly launched BIS Registration Scheme, 23 outside laboratories
have been recognized for testing electronic and IT products.
HALLMARKING
Hallmarking of gold jewellery was started by BIS in April 2000 to provide third party assurance
to consumers on the purity of gold jewellery or its fineness. The scheme for Hallmarking of
silver jewellery/ artefacts was launched in October 2005. As on 31 March 2016, the number
2
of operative licences for Hallmarking of gold and silver jewellery were 14820 and 1067
respectively. The number of operative BIS recognized Assaying & Hallmarking (A&H) centres
was 370. During the year, about 3.49 crore articles of gold and silver jewellery/ artefacts were
hallmarked and 36 jewellers’ awareness programmes were organized by BIS.
Gold Monetization Scheme
Ministry of Finance has launched Gold Monetization Scheme on 5th Nov.2015. BIS has
played an important role in finalization and implementation of the Gold Monetization Scheme
(GMS) in association with Department of Economic Affairs and Reserve Bank of India. Under
the scheme Assaying & Hallmarking Centres recognized by BIS have been qualified to act
as Collection and Purity Testing Centres (CPTC) and the gold collected by CPTCs is refined
by refineries licensed by BIS. So far 47 A&H centres and one jeweller have been qualified to
act as CPTC. Also, licenses have been granted to eight refineries for refining of gold under
the GMS.
Indian Gold Coin
Hon’ble Prime Minister released on 5th November 2015 the first ever National Gold Coin with
National emblem of Ashok Chakra engraved on one side and the face of Mahatma Gandhi
on the other side. It is a matter of pride for BIS that the coin is engraved with BIS Hallmark.
For manufacturing this hallmarked coin of 999 purity, the India Government mint, Mumbai
and India Government mint, Kolkata were granted license as per IS 1417:1999 during 2015-
16.
MANAGEMENT SYSTEM CERTIFICATION
BIS is operating various Management Systems Certification schemes. During 2015-16 BIS
has granted 43 Quality Management System Certification licences, 8 Environmental
Management Systems Certification licences, 18 Occupational Health & Safety Management
Systems Certification licences, 2 Food Safety Management System Certification licence, 37
Service Quality Management System Certification licences and 6 Energy Management
System Certification licences. As on 31 March 2016, the total number of operative licences
was 1336.
INTERNATIONAL ACTIVITIES AND TECHNICAL INFORMATION
SERVICES
BIS in its capacity as the National Standards Body of India, is a member of International
Organization for Standardization (ISO) and International Electro-technical Commission (IEC)
and actively participates in the activities of these International bodies. It is actively involved
in development of International Standards by acting as Participating (P) member or Observer
(O) member on various technical committees and sub-committees; and nominating technical
experts in working groups. As on 31 March 2016, BIS is a ‘P’ member in 418 Technical
Committees/ Subcommittees of ISO and 80 Technical Committees/Subcommittees of IEC.
3
Similarly BIS is ‘O’ Member in 224 Technical Committees/Subcommittees of ISO and 76
Technical Committees/ Subcommittees of IEC.
BIS is also engaged in regional and bilateral cooperation programmes pertaining to
standardization, testing, certification, training etc. So far, BIS has signed 28 Memorandum of
Understanding (MoUs) and 5 Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) with National
Standards Bodies of different countries.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION SERVICES
BIS provides technical information services to industry, importers, exporters, individuals and
government agencies in response to their enquiries. Around 1900 enquiries were responded
to during the period April 2015 to March 2016.
TRAINING SERVICES
During the year, National Institute of Training for Standardization (NITS) organized 111
programmes for industry, 3 International training programmes and 21 programmes for BIS
employees.
CONSUMER AFFAIRS
BIS endeavours to provide its services and the benefits of standardization and certification
to all its stakeholders in a focused and time bound manner. The Consumer Affairs department
of BIS handles various consumer related activities which include redressal of public
grievances and organizing various awareness programmes for the stakeholders.
During the year, 166 consumer awareness programmes, 49 industry awareness programmes
and 30 Education utilization of standard programmes were organized. BIS carried out 128
search and seizures all over the country on firms misusing ISI mark.
PUBLICITY
The publicity activity of BIS is aimed at creating awareness about various BIS activities
among the industry and the consumer, mainly relating to standardization, certification of
goods & services and Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery. The penal provision for unscrupulous
practices like spurious marking was also publicized during the year to deter violators. The
publicity during 2015-16 was done through print, electronic and other media like outdoor
publicity, metro rail, Rail Sampark 139, public utilities and hoardings at airports and railway
stations, cinema halls, etc.
4
SALE OF STANDARDS AND OTHER PUBLICATIONS
BIS sells Indian Standards and Special publications through 24 different sales outlets located
at the Headquarters (HQs), Regional offices and Branch Offices. Sale is also done through
registered booksellers. BIS also sells foreign standards like ISO, IEC, BSI London, DIN
Germany, JIS Japan in India. BIS sells Indian Standards through its e-portal and through
DVDs.
HINDI ACTIVITIES
BIS is following all the directions issued by the Department of Official Language regarding
use of Hindi and related activities. Official Language Committee of BIS HQ conducted all its
four quarterly meetings on time. The Second Sub Committee of Committee of Parliament on
Official Language inspected Vishakhapatnam, Rajkot and Mumbai offices during 2015-16.
During the period, 68 standards were translated and titles of 670 standards were also made
bilingual.
PLAN SCHEMES
Hallmarking
BIS has been implementing the plan scheme for setting up of A&H Centres with central
assistance. The scheme of hallmarking is operative since Xth Plan and has also continued
in the XIIth Plan. The components of the scheme includes infrastructure building through
setting up of A&H Centres in deficient locations and capacity building by way of providing
training to artisans, auditors and other personnel engaged in hallmarking related activities.
During 2015-16, BIS received Rs.375 lakhs under the Plan scheme from the Government
and spent Rs.372.69 lakhs. Seven artisan training programmes, one training of trainers
programme and four A&H personnel training programmes were conducted during 2015-16.
National System for Standardization
The scheme of National System of Standardization (NSS) is to promote participation of
experts in National and International standardisation. The Plan funds under the scheme are
also utilized for organising ISO/IEC technical committee meetings and for holding various
training seminars, workshops etc.
5
PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND WORKS
The works relating to construction of new office buildings of BIS at various places and
renovation works in existing buildings were undertaken during 2015-16.
BIS has also undertaken a 'green' initiative under which projects for installation of Rooftop
solar power plants in BIS buildings are being undertaken through the Solar Energy
Corporation of India.
HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT, ADMINISTRATION AND
GENERAL SERVICES
Recruitment - During the year, 71 scientists were recruited for the post of Scientist-B through
direct recruitment. As on 31 March 2016, a total of 1532 persons were on roll in BIS.
Swachh Bharat Mission - Special cleanliness drive was undertaken in all offices of BIS
during 22 June 2015 to 15 August 2015 as per instructions received from Department of
Consumer Affairs.
Staff Welfare - BIS continued its welfare measures for its employees, namely, Group
Insurance Scheme, facility of holiday homes, in-house service of a part-time doctor at HQ,
subsidized refreshment, children scholarship scheme etc.
Library Services - BIS technical Library located at headquarters is a national resources
centre for information on standards and related matters and meets the needs of industry,
trade, government, researchers and consumers alike.
Constitution of Complaints Committee on Sexual Harassment of Women at Work Place
In compliance with the guidelines of the Supreme Court of India on the prevention of sexual
harassment of women at the work place, an Internal Complaints Committees have been
constituted in BIS offices at New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Chandigarh.
FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
For the Twenty Seventh consecutive year i.e. 2015-16, BIS continued to be self-reliant in
meeting its expenditure and other liabilities. Total income (excluding income from
investment) during the year 2015-16 amounted to Rs. 39082.83 lakh as against Rs. 34542.86
lakh in the previous year making an increase of 13.14%. The largest contribution to the
income was from product certification marking Fee which stood at Rs. 32611.05 lakh during
2015-16 against Rs. 30252.43 lakh in 2014-15 an increase of 7.80%. The total revenue
expenditure during the year 2015-16 amounted to Rs. 23503.26 lakh as against Rs. 21095.90
lakh in 2014-15 registering an increase of 11.41%.
6

BIS  ANNUAL REPORT 2019-20 iii
OVERVIEW
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the National Standards Body of India was
established under the BIS Act 1986, assuming the functions of the erstwhile
Indian Standards Institution (ISI). BIS Act 2016 came into force on 12 October 2017
superseding BIS Act 1986. BIS Act 2016 provides for the establishment of a national
standards body for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization,
conformity assessment and quality assurance of goods, articles, processes, systems
and services and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
With the integration of global economies, countries around the world are strategically
positioning themselves at international level to gain competitive edge and achieve
economic benefits. As standards and conformity assessment are significantly influencing
global trade, countries are therefore adopting strategies to seek positions in international
standardization fora to influence international standards in their favour. India in tandem
with National standardization strategies is interacting with various industry associations
to harness Indian skills and strength and review the existing standards and make forays
into new avenues relevant from the view point of standardization.
Standardization supports economic growth, enhances competitiveness and fosters
technological developments. It is also a tool to influence public policies such as health
and safety, protection of environment and consumer protection. By ensuring a level
playing field and defining common criteria of acceptance of goods, standards are
increasingly being used as tools to support regulatory framework and to facilitate trade.
In this regard, BIS is fruitfully interacting with various stakeholders to bring a number
of products under mandatory certification thereby ensuring protection of consumers’
interest.
BIS through its core activities of standardization and conformity assessment, has been
benefiting the national economy by providing safe, reliable and quality goods; minimizing
health hazards to consumers; protecting the environment, promoting exports and imports
substitute; controlling over proliferation of varieties etc. The standards and certification
scheme of BIS apart from benefitting the consumers and industry also support various
public policies especially in areas of product safety, consumer protection, food safety,
environment protection, building and construction, etc.
During the year, BIS worked towards specifically addressing various national priorities
and other Govt. initiatives in the areas of formulation of standards in twelve champion
service sectors, medical textiles, testing of quality of piped drinking water, mandatory
hallmarking of gold jewellery to name a few. In standards development, BIS continued to
address issues of technology changes and advancements, climate change, environment
and energy conservation, conditions of health and safety and facilitation of trade. In the
area of conformity assessment BIS worked towards making the processes simpler and
faster. BIS maintained a satisfactory progress in all its activities during the year.

ORGANIZATIONAL
NETWORK
BIS has its Headquarters at New Delhi. It has 5 Regional Offices (ROs) located at Kolkata (Eastern),
Mumbai (Western), Chandigarh (Northern), Chennai (Southern), and Delhi (Central). Under the
Regional Offices are the Branch Offices (BOs). There are 32 BOs located at 28 different locations
namely Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Chennai, Coimbatore,
Dehradun, Delhi, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Guwahati, Hubli, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu,
Jamshedpur, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Parwanoo, Patna, Pune, Raipur, Rajkot
and Vishakhapatnam. The BOs serve as an effective link between State Governments, industries,
technical institutions, consumer organizations, etc., of the region.
To cater to the needs of testing of samples, BIS has eight laboratories in the country namely
Central Laboratory (CL), Sahibabad; Eastern Regional Office Laboratory (EROL), Kolkata; Western
Regional Office Laboratory (WROL), Mumbai; Northern Regional Office Laboratory (NROL),
Mohali; Southern Regional Office Laboratory (SROL), Chennai; Bangalore Branch Office Laboratory
(BNBOL), Bengaluru; Patna Branch Office Laboratory (PBOL),
Patna; Guwahati Branch Office Laboratory (GBOL),
Guwahati.

clause_title: Preamble
text:
REVIEW OF BIS ANNUAL REPORT 2016-17
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the National Standard Body of India was established
under the BIS Act 1986, assuming the functions of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution
(ISI). BIS is responsible for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization,
marking and quality certification of goods and for matters connected therewith or incidental
thereto.
STANDARDIZATION
The process of standards development adopted by BIS follows internationally accepted good
standardization practices and in compliance with the WTO-TBT code of good practice for
preparation, adoption and application of standards. In the development of National
Standards, BIS provides all interested stakeholders, with a neutral platform to come together
and work towards common agreements. BIS currently provides a forum for 325 Sectional
Committees, representing over a thousand experts from organized consumers & consumer
bodies, regulatory and other government bodies, industries, scientists, technologists, testing
organizations and individual experts. Also includes concerned officials of BIS. These
committees work cooperatively to develop consensus based voluntary National standards
with stakeholder consultations.
A total of 286 Technical committee meetings were held during 2016-17, to consider draft
standards and related technical documents in detail. It is the policy of BIS to formulate Indian
Standards on emerging technologies and to withdraw obsolete standards.
During 2016-17, 722 (new 371 and revised 351) standards were formulated. The total
number of standards in force, as on 31 March 2017 was 19025.
CERTIFICATION
BIS operates a Product Certification Scheme under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986
and the Rules and Regulations framed there-under. Under this Certification scheme, a
manufacturer of a particular product is given the self marking rights of the BIS standards
mark (ISI mark) on his product after ensuring that his product complies with the relevant
Indian Standard. Presence of Standard Mark (popularly known as ISI mark) on a product
indicates its conformity to the relevant Indian Standard. The certification scheme is voluntary
in nature, except for 109 product standards that have been made mandatory by the Central
Government on considerations of health and safety of the consumer.
During the year, 4098 new licences were granted, which include 17 products covered for the
first time under the scheme. The total number of Indian Standards which have been covered
so far under BIS Certification Marks Scheme are 927. The total number of operative licences
as on 31 March 2016 was 31347 which increased to 33230 by March 2017.
Surveillance
In order to monitor the operation of licences, during the year, a total number of 10162
inspections and 8256 lot inspections were carried out. In addition, about 21384 samples
(including samples procured from market) were drawn for independent testing.
Foreign Manufactures Certification Scheme (FMCS)
BIS has been operating separate Scheme for foreign manufacturers. Under this Scheme,
foreign manufacturers can seek certification from BIS for use of BIS Standard Mark on their
product(s). During 2016-17, 190 licences were issued under FMCS, taking the total number
of operative licences to 671 against 83 Indian Standards. The licences granted covered
products such as Steel & Steel products; Cement; PVC Insulated Cables; Tyres & Tubes for
Automotive Vehicles; Plastic Feeding Bottles; Switchgear products; Plugs & Socket-Outlets
and Switches; HDPE & UPVC Pipes; Infant milk formula; ac Static Energy Meters etc. from
around 48 countries across the globe.
Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS)
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), then known as Department
of Electronics & Information Technology (DeitY), in consultation with BIS, notified ‘Electronics
and Information Technology Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order,
2012’ on 3 October 2012 mandating Compulsory Registration from BIS for 15 Electronics
and Information Technology products based on its safety compliance to Indian Standards. A
second Order was notified on 13 November 2014, bringing 15 more electronics and
Information Technology products under the ambit of the Scheme. The Compulsory
Registration Scheme is being operated by BIS under the BIS Act, 1986 and the Rules, framed
thereunder for this purpose.
The first Registration was granted by BIS in June 2013. As on 31 March 2017, BIS has
granted 8316 registrations to manufacturers in various countries including domestic
manufacturers.
LABORATORY SERVICES
In order to support the activities of the product certification marks scheme, BIS has
established eight laboratories in the country to cater to the testing need of samples generated
from Product Certification Scheme, beginning with the establishment of Central Laboratory
at Sahibabad in 1962. Subsequently, four regional laboratories at Mohali, Kolkata, Mumbai
and Chennai and three branch office laboratories at Patna, Bangalore and Guwahati were
established. BIS laboratories have facilities for testing of products in chemical,
microbiological, electrical and mechanical discipline.
BIS labs have complete test facilities for 376 Indian Standards and partial test facilities for
358 Indian Standards. During the year, the BIS laboratories tested 18502 samples of various
products covered under BIS Certification. In addition, the Gold Referral Assaying Laboratory
at Chennai has issued 2965 test reports during the year.
Lab Recognition Scheme
As the volume of work for testing of samples generated from product certification scheme is
much larger than the available facilities and capacity in BIS labs, BIS has established
Laboratory Recognition Scheme (LRS) for recognition of outside laboratories (OSLs). The
services of such laboratories are utilized when it is economically not viable to develop test
facilities in BIS labs or when BIS labs are overloaded.
During 2016-17, 25 new labs were recognized and 6 labs were de-recognized. As on 31
March 2017, the total number of operative BIS recognized labs were 179, which included
reputed R&D organizations, technical institutions, Government labs and Private sector labs.
Besides this, services of 47 Government laboratories of specialized nature are utilized for
different products, as and when required.
To support the newly launched BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme, 33 outside labs are
testing IT products, which were covered under Electronics and Information Technology
Goods (Requirement for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012 of Ministry of Electronics and
Information Technology (MeitY).
HALLMARKING
Hallmarking of gold jewellery was launched by BIS in April 2000 to provide third party
assurance to consumers on the purity of gold jewellery or its fineness. The scheme for
Hallmarking of silver jewellery/ artefacts was launched in October 2005. Under these Scheme,
while the jewellers are granted licence to sell hallmarked jewellery, Assaying & Hallmarking
(A&H) centres are recognized to assay the purity of the jewellery submitted by the licensed
jeweller, along with declaration of purity.
As on 31 March 2017, the number of operative licences for Hallmarking of gold and silver
jewellery were 18112 and 1494 respectively. The number of operative BIS recognized A&H
centres was 454. During the year, 3.16 crore articles of gold and silver jewellery/ artefacts
were hallmarked.
Hallmark of Gold Bullion/Coin
Hallmarking of gold Bullion/Coin in the fineness of 999 & 995 by giving licence to
refineries/Mint was started in October 2015. During 2016-17, two licences have been granted
to the refineries for the hallmarking of gold Bullions/Coins. As on 31 March 2017, 10 licences
have been granted to refineries/ India Government Mint for Gold bullion and coin.
GOLD MONETIZATION SCHEME
Government of India has launched Gold Monetization Scheme on 5 November 2015. BIS
has played an important role in finalization and implementation of the Gold Monetization
Scheme in association with Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance and
Reserve Bank of India. Under the scheme A&H Centres recognized by BIS have been
qualified to act as Collection and Purity Testing Centres (CPTC). So far 48 A&H centres and
one Jeweller have been qualified to act as CPTC. The gold collected by CPTCs is to be
refined by refineries licenced by BIS.
Promotion of Hallmarking
To promote hallmarking in the country for effective consumer protection in purchase of gold
jewellery, awareness programmes for jewellers are organized by BIS through its various
Regional and Branch offices across the country. During 2016-17, 53 such jewellers’
awareness programmes were organized.
MANAGEMENT SYSTEM CERTIFICATION
BIS is operating various Management Systems Certification schemes and licences granted
as on 31 March 2017, 867 Quality Management System Certification (QMS) licences, 203
Environmental Management Systems (EMS) Certification licences, 102 Occupational Health
& Safety Management Systems (OHSMS) Certification licences, two Hazards Analysis and
Critical Control Point (HACCP) stand-alone licences, 35 HACCP licences integrated with
QMS, 14 Food Safety Management System (FSMS) licences, 101 Service Quality
Management System (SQMS) licences, 20 Energy Management System (EnMS) licences
and one Medical Devices Management System (MDMS) licences were in operation.
INTERNATIONAL ACTIVITIES AND TECHNICAL INFORMATION SERVICES
 BIS in its capacity as the National Standards Body of India, is a member of International
Organization for Standardization (ISO) and through the Indian National Committee a
member of International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). BIS actively participates in
the activities of these International bodies and is involved in development of International
Standards as Participating (P) member or Observer (O) member on various Technical
Committees and Sub-Committees; and nominates technical experts in Working Groups
of these bodies. As on 31 March 2017, BIS is a ‘P’ member in 433 Technical Committees/
Subcommittees of ISO and 86 Technical Committees/Subcommittees of IEC, and ‘O’
Member in 219 Technical Committees/Subcommittees of ISO and 72 Technical
Committees/ Subcommittees of IEC. The Secretariat of 8 important ISO Committees
dealing with subjects that are of interest to India are being held by India through BIS.
BIS has entered into Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) and Mutual Recognition
Agreements (MRAs) with the National Standards Bodies of various countries for cooperation
in the areas of standards, Conformity assessment, testing and training/ capacity building and
for mutual acceptance of each other’s conformity assessment results respectively. BIS has
so far signed 32 MoUs and 6 MRAs of which 7 MoUs and 1 MRA were concluded during
2016-17.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION SERVICES & WTO-TBT ENQUIRY POINT
BIS provides technical information services in the field of standards and conformity
assessment to industry, importers, exporters and government agencies in response to their
enquiries. 1079 enquiries were responded during the period from April 2016 to March 2017.
Sponsorship of Identification Numbers
 Issuer Identification Number (IIN)
BIS facilitates issue of IINs as per ISO/IEC 7812 ‘Identification Cards - Identification of
issuers’ by sponsoring applications of Banks/ Financial Organizations to the American
Bankers Association (ABA). The ISO/IEC 7812 specifies a numbering system for the
identification of issuers of the identification cards used in international and/ or inter-industry
interchange. During this period, BIS had taken up the application of M/s National Payment
Cooperation of India (NPCI), (an autonomous body set up by the Reserve Bank of India as
an Umbrella organization for retail payments in India) for allotment of 3000 IINs under Card
Scheme Block Holder, for enabling them to further the Government of India initiative of Digital
India.
 World Manufacturer Identifier (WMI) Number
In co-ordination with the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE), USA; BIS issues WMI
Codes as per ISO 3780 : 2009 ‘Road Vehicles - World Manufacturer Identifier (WMI) Code’
to automobile manufacturers and exporters in India. 180 WMI Codes have been allotted to
various vehicle manufacturers during 2016-17.
TRAINING SERVICES
National Institute of Training for Standardization (NITS) was set up under the aegis of BIS in
1995 to meet the growing needs and expectations of the industry for quality training in the
fields of standardization, quality assurance, management systems, certification, laboratory
testing, etc. NITS has also been organizing various International Training Programmes for
the developing countries of Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin and South America. The
programmes are conducted by a team of well-experienced, qualified and trained faculty.
During year 2016-17, NITS conducted a number of training programmes for the Industry,
International participants and BIS employees. There has been an increase in the number of
programmes organized during the period as well as the number of persons trained vis-à-vis
the number of programmes carried out and the number of persons trained in the previous
years. The total number of programmes conducted during this period is 177. The number of
personnel trained during 2016-17 for the industry was 2355 which is about 13.5% more than
the last year figures of 2075.
CONSUMER AFFAIRS
BIS endeavours to provide its services and the benefits of standardization and certification
to all its stakeholders in a focused manner. The Consumer Affairs department of BIS handles
various consumer related activities which include redressal of public grievances, organizing
various awareness programmes for the stakeholders of BIS and holding of World Standards
Day.
During the year, 163 consumer awareness programmes, 62 Industry awareness
programmes, 39 Educational Utilization of Standards Programmes were organized across
the country.
World Standards Day :
BIS celebrated the World Standards Day on 14 October 2016 at New Delhi to pay tribute to
the collaborative efforts of thousands of experts worldwide, who develop voluntary technical
agreements that are published as International or National Standards. The World Standards
Day theme for the year 2016 was ‘Standards Build Trust’. BIS on the occasion also organized
a seminar on this theme. World Standards Day programmes were also held across the
country by BIS Regional and Branch Offices.
PUBILCITY
The publicity activity of BIS is aimed at creating awareness for various BIS activities among
its target audience including the Industry and common Consumer, significantly relating to
Standardization, Certification of goods & services and Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery. The
publicity was done through print, electronic and outdoor media.
Aggressive publicity campaigns were taken up aiming at persuading consumers to buy ISI
Marked goods and Hallmarked Gold Jewellery. Consumers were also informed about the
mechanism regarding the redressal of complaints relating to BIS. BIS also participated in
popular consumer and industrial fairs/exhibitions to disseminate information on the various
activities of BIS.
SALE OF STANDARDS AND OTHER PUBLICATIONS
BIS sells Indian Standards and Special Publications through 25 different sales outlets located
at the Headquarters (HQs), Regional Offices and Branch Offices. Sale is also done through
registered booksellers. BIS also sells foreign standards (ISO, IEC, BSI London, DIN
Germany, JIS Japan) in India. BIS also sells Indian Standards through e-portal. Standards
can be downloaded in the form of soft copy. Alternatively, an order for hard copy can be
placed through the e-portal. Online payment can be made over the portal through credit/debit
card. Customers can also make payment for standards through NEFT/RTGS.
HINDI ACTIVITIES
BIS is following all the act, rules, directions and orders issued by the Department of Official
Language regarding official language. Official Language Committee of HQ conducted all its
four quarterly meetings on time. The Second Sub Committee of Committee of Parliament on
Official Language inspected Headquarter on 18 February 2017. The Committee expressed
satisfaction over the progressive use of Hindi in BIS. During the year, 53 standards were
translated and titles of 540 standards were also made bilingual.
PLAN SCHEMES
Hallmarking:
BIS has been implementing the Plan scheme for setting up of gold Assaying and Hallmarking
(A&H) centres in India with central assistance. The scheme on Hallmarking, operative since
the Xth Plan has continued in the XIIth Plan.
During 2016-17, BIS received ₹ 117.8 lakhs and ₹ 32.2 lakhs carry-over of pervious year
(total amount 150 lakhs) under this scheme and spent ₹ 147 lakhs. Sixteen artisan training
programmes, six A&H personnel training programmes and three Training of Trainers
programme were conducted.
National System for Standardization:
The scheme on National System of Standardization (NSS) which commenced during the XIth
Plan has continued to operate in the XIIth Plan.
During 2016-17, BIS has spent about Rs. 164.53 lakhs and no grant received for NSS
activities.
INFORMATION TECHNOILOGY SERVICES
In line with the Government’s initiatives for computerization and to make day to day
functioning of BIS online, IT is being enabled as a strategic resource for development and
continual improvement of systems. The overall objective is to improve services by increasing
efficiency, transparency and ensuring reliability and timely delivery to BIS stakeholders.
PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND WORKS
The works relating to construction of new office buildings for BIS Offices and renovation
works in existing buildings is undertaken by Project Management and Works Department
(PMWD) of BIS.
PMWD has also undertaken a 'green' initiative under which projects for installation of Rooftop
Solar Power Plants in BIS buildings are being undertaken through the Solar Energy
Corporation of India.
VIGILANCE ACTIVITIES
The vigilance set up of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is headed by the Chief Vigilance
Officer (CVO) and comprises of Vigilance Department at BIS Headquarters and a Vigilance
Section in the Secretariat of each of the Disciplinary Authority for Group B, C & D employees
(Deputy Director General concerned).
The Vigilance Department functions in close coordination with Central Vigilance Commission
(CVC), Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) and Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food &
Public Distribution. It is entrusted with the responsibility of managing all vigilance related
activities of the Bureau in accordance with the guidelines on the subject issued by Central
Vigilance Commission and DoPT etc.
HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT, ADMINISTRATION AND
GENERAL SERVICES
Recruitment - During the year, 13 scientists in waiting list of the recruitment process of
2015-16 joined as Scientist-B through direct recruitment.
Swachh Bharat Mission - The Swachh Bharat drive was carried out in BIS in two phases
i.e. 16– 31 May 2016 & 16 – 31 October 2016.
Staff Welfare - BIS continued its welfare measures for its employees namely by way of
Group Insurance Schemes, facility of Holiday Homes, subsidized refreshments, provision of
newspapers at the reception counter and to officers of the level of Deputy Director General
and above, Children Scholarship Scheme, etc.
Library Services - BIS technical Library located at Headquarters is a national resources
centre for information on standards and related matters and meets the needs of industry,
trade, government, researchers and consumers alike.
SEXUAL HARASSMENT OF WORKING WOMEN AT WORKPLACE - In compliance with
the guidelines of the Supreme Court of India on the prevention of sexual harassment of
women at work place, an Internal Complaints Committee at BIS Headquarters was
constituted under Section 4 of (i) Rule 3-C and Government of India’s Decisions (25) under
said Rule of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964; (ii) Sexual Harassment of
Women at Work Place [Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal] Act, April 2013; and (iii)
Sexual Harassment of Women at Work Place (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules,
December 2013; and re-constituted on 5 November 2015 for a period of two years. The
composition of the newly constituted Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) at BIS
Headquarters consists of a senior level women employee as Presiding Officer and three
other members including one member from All India Democratic Women’s Association
(AIDWA), New Delhi. In addition, ICCs have also been constituted in the four Regional
Offices at Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai & Chandigarh.
FINANCE ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
For the Twenty Eighth consecutive year i.e. 2016-17, Bureau of Indian Standards continued
to be self reliant in meeting its expenditure and other liabilities. Total income (excluding
income from investment) during the year 2016-17 amounted to Rs. 45663.38 lakh as against
Rs. 39082.83 lakh in the previous year resulting in an increase of 16.84%. The largest
contribution to the income was from Product Certification Marking Fee which stood at Rs.
38930.80 lakh against Rs. 32611.05 lakh in the previous year i.e. an increase of 19.38%.
The total revenue expenditure during the year 2016-17 amounted to Rs. 21633.58 lakh as
against Rs. 21001.20 lakh in 2015-16 registering a increase of 3.01%.

text:
REVIEW OF BIS ANNUAL REPORT 2014-15
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) was set up on 01 April 1987 as a statutory body,
taking over the functions of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution (ISI). Its major activities
include Formulation of Standards, Product Certification, Hallmarking, various Management
Systems Certification Schemes, Laboratory Services, Sale of Indian Standards and Training
services. Besides, it is also engaged in Consumer related and Promotional Activities.
Major achievements of BIS during the year 2014-15, as reported in its Annual Report are
summarized below:
STANDARDIZATION
BIS is formulating need-based Indian standards in line with the National Priorities in a time-
bound manner. It also harmonizes National Standards with International Standards in order
to facilitate adoption of International Standards by all segments of industry and business.
During 2014-15, BIS formulated 746 standards bringing the total number of standards in
force to 19295 as on 31 March 2015. In addition, 3228 standards were reviewed. 5249
Indian standards have been harmonized with International Standards so far. During the year,
BIS also organized 12 Seminars/ Workshops and participated in Conferences with a view to
disseminate information about the availability of standards and to get feedback for further
improvement/ updating as well as to find out fields where standardization is needed by the
industry.
CERTIFICATION
PRODUCT CERTIFICATION
During the year 2014-15, BIS has granted 3202 new licences (excluding hallmarking). The
total number of operative licences as on 31 March 2014 was 29516. Ten new products were
covered for the first time under product certification. Under foreign manufacturers’
certification scheme, 111 licences were granted, thus making a total of 470 licences located
in various countries.
Registration Scheme
Registration Scheme is being operated by BIS as per BIS Rules - Chapter IV A
“REGISTRATION”. The Department of Electronics and Information Technology, Ministry of
Communication & Information Technology, had issued “Electronics and Information
Technology Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012” notifying 15
products for compulsory registration w.e.f. 03 April 2013. Govt. of India, has notified 15 more
Electronics and IT goods during Nov 2014, taking the total number of products under this
scheme to 30. As on 31 Mar 2015, a total of 1428 registrations have been granted to
manufacturers located throughout the world for the above mentioned products.
Review Meetings
In order to acquire feedback on the operation of the BIS Certification Marks Scheme, review
meetings with the licensees are organized on a regular basis. In 2014-15, 60 review
meetings were organized.
LABORATORY SERVICES
The network of eight BIS laboratories located in different regions of the country continued to
undertake conformity testing of BIS certified products against relevant Indian standards. The
number of samples tested by BIS Laboratories was 14966. Gold Referral Assaying
Laboratory at Chennai started since December 2010, has issued 1174 test reports during
2014-15. As on March 2015, 143 outside labs stood recognised by BIS.
BIS Lab Recognition Scheme
BIS lab recognition scheme supports operation of product certification scheme of BIS. The
services of outside laboratories are availed in an eventuality of heavy load for testing in BIS
Labs, any equipment being out of order or test facility not being there. As on 31 March 2015,
there were 143 outside laboratories recognized by BIS. Besides, facilities of 46 Government
laboratories (specialized labs/ other labs) are being utilized by BIS as and when required. To
support newly launched BIS Registration Scheme, 93 outside labs were recognized for
testing of IT products.
HALLMARKING OF JEWELLERY/ ARTEFACTS
The Scheme for Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery, which was successfully launched by BIS in
April 2000, continued to make considerable progress. 1995 Gold hallmarking licences and
176 Silver hallmarking licences have been granted during the year. The number of operative
licences for Hallmarking of gold and silver jewellery was 13112 and 936 respectively, as on

clause_title: March 2015. The number of BIS recognized assaying and hallmarking centres was 331
text:
as on 31 March 2015. Regional and Branch offices of BIS organized 40 Awareness
programmes for jewellers.
MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS CERTIFICATION
BIS continued to provide the following Management Systems Certification services as per the
corresponding standards. 53 Quality Management System Certification licences, 27
Environmental Management Systems Certification licences, 13 Occupational Health & Safety
Management Systems Certification licences, 01 Food Safety Management System
Certification licence, 17 Service Quality Management System Certification licences and 06
Energy Management System Certification licences were granted during the year. As on 31
March 2015, the total number of operative licences was 1295.
INTERNATIONAL ACTIVITIES
BIS, in its capacity as the National Standards Body of India, is a member of International
Organization for Standardization (ISO) and International Electro-technical Commission (IEC).
It is actively involved in the development of International Standards by acting as Participating
(P) member or Observer (O) member on various Technical Committees, Sub-Committees,
Working Groups, etc.
2
BIS was also actively involved in the Regional and Bi-lateral Co-operation Programmes
pertaining to standardization, testing, certification, training etc. So far, BIS has signed
MoU/MRA with national standards bodies of 26 countries.
Information services
Technical Information Service Centre
Technical Information Services are provided to Industry, importers, exporters, individuals and
government agencies in response to their enquiries. In this endeavour, more than 400
enquiries were responded during the year 2014-15.
WTO/TBT Enquiry Point
BIS continued its activities as the WTO / TBT Enquiry Point. BIS worked in close interaction
with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on various issues of national interest. All valid
queries pertaining to Standards and Conformity Assessment systems, both national and of
other countries were replied.
TRAINING SERVICES
During 2014-15, National Institute of Training for Standardization (NITS) organized 53 In-
house programmes, 49 Open programmes including 7 Lead Auditors courses for the
industry, 4 programs for consumer organizations and 5 programs for Technical Commitee
Members & Standards Developing Organizations under XII plan thus generating revenue of
around Rs. 3.62 crores. Besides above, 04 International Training Programmes and 21
programmes for BIS employees were also organised
CONSUMER AFFAIRS
BIS endeavours to provide its services and the benefits of standardization and certification to
all its stakeholders in a focused, time bound manner and satisfactory manner. The
department handles consumer related activities which includes organizing various awareness
programmes for the stakeholders of BIS, organising Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Award and
World Standards Day.
Standards Promotion and Consumer Affairs
During the year, 292 consumer awareness programs, 113 Industry awareness programs and

clause_title: programs for educational utilization of standards were organized. 96 grievances/
text:
complaints were received and 80 grievances/complaints were redressed.
Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Award
With a view to encourage manufacturers and service organizations to strive for excellence,
Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Award was instituted by the Bureau in 1991. The awards for
Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Awards for the year 2012 were announced by the Hon’ble
Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India. The
awards announced included ‘Best of All Award’ and 03 Category awards (01 Large Scale
Manufacturing Industry, 01 Large Scale Service Industry and 01 Small Scale Manufacturing
3
Industry) and 09 Commendation Certificates. The fact finding and evaluation process for
RGNQA 2013 is in progress.
World Standards Day
World Standards Day was celebrated on 14 October 2014 to commemorate the
establishment of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The theme of this
year World Standards Day was “Standards level the playing field”.
Enforcement
During the year, 67 enforcement raids were carried out all over India on firms misusing the
BIS Standard Mark. 18 cases filed in court were decided, all were decided in favour of BIS.
XIIth PLAN PROJECTS
BIS is implementing following 02 Central Sector Schemes under XIIth Five year Plan (2012-
17), as approved by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution:
i. Gold Hallmarking
ii. National System for Standardization
VIGILANCE ACTIVITIES
The vigilance Set up of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is headed by the Chief Vigilance
Officer (CVO) and comprises of Vigilance Department at BIS Headquarters. During 2014-15,
a two-day training programme on Preventive Vigilance for the senior officers of BIS was
conducted for each of the five regions at NITS, NOIDA, WRO, Mumbai, SRO, Chennai, NRO,
Chandigarh and ERO, Kolkata during the year. 78 Senior Officers of BIS participated in these
five training programmes. The Vigilance Awareness Week was celebrated in Bureau of
Indian Standards from 27 October 2014 to 01 November 2014.
HUMAN RESOURCES
During the year, 67 scientists were recruited for the post of Scientist-B by direct recruitment.
As on 31 March 2015, a total of 1532 persons were on roll in BIS.
INCOME AND EXPENDITURE
For the Twenty Sixth consecutive year i.e. 2014-15, Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
continued to be self reliant in meeting its expenditure and other liabilities. Total income
(excluding income from investment) during the year 2014-15 was Rs. 34542.86 lakh as
against Rs.31443.12 lakh in the previous year, resulting in an increase of 9.86%. The largest
contribution to the income was from ISI Certification Marking Fee which stood at Rs.
30813.14 lakh against Rs. 27949.15 lakh in the previous year i.e. an increase of 10.25%. The
total revenue expenditure during the year 2014-15 was Rs. 18765.93 lakh as against Rs.
18656.30 lakh in 2013-14 registering a marginal increase of 0.59%.
4

clause_title: Accreditation - The laboratory shall be accredited to Laboratory Quality Management

clause_title: Preamble
text:
REVIEW OF BIS ANNUAL REPORT 2011-12
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) was set up on 1 April 1987 as a statutory body, taking
over the functions of the erstwhile Indian Standards Institution (ISI). Its major activities
include Formulation of Standards, Product Certification, Hallmarking, various Management
Systems Certification Schemes, Laboratory Services, Sale of Indian Standards and Training
services. Besides, it is also engaged in Consumer related and Promotional Activities.
Major achievements of BIS during the year 2011-12, as reported in its Annual Report for this
period are summarized below.
FORMULATION AND REVIEW OF STANDARDS
During 2011-12, BIS formulated 410 standards bringing the total number of standards in
force to 18742 as on 31 March 2012. In addition, 3784 standards were reviewed. 5091
Indian standards have been harmonized with International Standards so far (i.e. about 88%
where corresponding ISO/IEC standards exist). In all 26 Seminars/ Conferences/ Workshops
were conducted to disseminate information on standards available in the specific fields for
increased implementation.
PRODUCT CERTIFICATION
During the year 2011-12, BIS has granted 3099 new licences (excluding hallmarking). The
total number of operative licences as on 31 March 2012 was 25330. During the year, 11 new
products were covered for the first time under product certification.
Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme
BIS is operating two schemes for certification of imported goods, one for foreign
manufacturers and the other for Indian importers. During the year, 73 licences were granted
to foreign manufacturers making the total of 232 licences located in various countries.
Review Meetings
In order to acquire feedback on the operation of the BIS Certification Marks Scheme, review
meetings with the licensees are organized on a regular basis. In 2011-12, 10 review
meetings were organized with licensees of Packaged Drinking Water; Steel and Steel
Products; Cement and Allied Products; Tyres; Electrical Cables and Conductors; LPG
Cylinders, Jute and Jute Products; Plastic Pipes and Plastic Related Products; Fire
Extinguishers; etc.
HALLMARKING OF JEWELLERY/ ARTEFACTS
The Scheme for Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery, which was successfully launched by BIS in
April 2000, continued to make considerable progress. Its simplification and rationalization has
resulted in an increase to 9292 jewellers as on 31 March 2012 from 8098 jewellers as on 31
March 2011. The number of silver licences for Hallmarking of silver jewellery/ artefacts has
increased from 495 to 580 during the year. The licensees could get their jewellery
hallmarked from 186 Assaying and Hallmarking Centres recognized by BIS. Around 250
lakhs articles of gold jewellery/ artefacts have been hallmarked during the year.
Awareness Programmes
Regional and Branch offices of BIS organized 40 Awareness programmes for jewellers. 5
Awareness Week Programmes were also organized in different states for Consumers.
MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS CERTIFICATION
Quality Management System Certification
During 2011-12, 119 Quality Management System Certification(QMSC) licences have been
granted, covering industrial sectors like chemicals, metal and metal products, cement,
construction, dairy plants, electricity generation, engineering services, mining, machinery,
petroleum, plastic, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and service sectors such as education, financial
sector, health sector, insurance, information technology, telecommunications, transport etc.
The total number of operative licences as on 31 March 2012 was 937.
Environmental Management System Certification
Environmental Management Systems Certification (EMSC) Scheme launched by BIS as per
IS/ISO 14001, continues to be popular. During the year, 16 EMSC licences have been
granted, making a total of 169 operative licences as on 31 March 2012 These licences cover
technology areas like Integrated Steel Plants, Thermal Power Plants, Aeronautical Industries,
Atomic Power Stations, Textiles, Plastic, Cement, Construction, Electrical And
Telecommunication Cables, Petroleum Refinery, Insecticides, Industrial And Explosive
Chemicals, Railway Wagon Workshops, Pharmaceuticals, Machinery, Mining, Public
Administration (Pollution Control Board) etc.
Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems (OHSMS) Certification
BIS launched OHSMS certification as per IS 18001:2000 in January 2003. It essentially
enables an organization to define, plan and manage its objectives and policies, taking into
account legislative requirements and information about significant hazards and risks, so as to
protect its employees and others, whose health and safety may be affected by the activities
of the organization. During the year, 9 OHSMS licences have been granted making the total
licences in operation as 56. The licences cover areas like Thermal Power Plants, Ceramic
Industry, Cycle Industry, Gas Power Station, Health Services and Employee Development
Centre.
Food Safety Management System (FSMS) and Service Quality Management Systems
(SQMS) Certification
BIS has also certification schemes running for Food Safety Management System as per
IS/ISO 22000:2005 and Service Quality Management Systems Certification as per IS
15700:2005 Quality Management Systems – Requirements for Service Delivery by Public
2
Service Organizations. 9 FSMS licences and 5 SQMS licences (17 Units) were under
operation as on 31 March 2012.
ENFORCEMENT ACTIVITIES
In order to protect the common consumer from being cheated by those misusing BIS
Standard Mark 125 raids were carried out all over the country. During these raids various
spurious products including many household products such as Packaged Drinking Water,
Block Board and Plywood products, PVC Cables, Switches & Sockets, Electrical Appliance,
Submersible pumps, Cement, Cattle feeds, Iodized salt, Steel Tubes, Cast Iron Sluice
Valves, LPG Regulators, HDPE Pipes etc. were seized.
LABORATORY SERVICES
The network of eight BIS laboratories located in different regions of the country continued to
undertake conformity testing of BIS certified products against relevant Indian standards.
During the year, 19005 test reports were issued by BIS laboratories covering wide range of
products. Gold Referral Assaying Laboratory at Chennai has issued 226 test reports from 1
April 2011 to 31 March 2012. It has also participated in Inter Laboratory Comparison
programme for testing of samples of Gold jewellery with satisfactory results.
BIS Lab Recognition Scheme
BIS lab recognition scheme supports operation of product certification scheme of BIS. The
services of outside laboratories are availed in an eventuality of heavy load for testing in BIS
Labs, any equipment being out of order or test facility not being there. As on as on 31 March
2012 there were 131 outside laboratories recognized by BIS. Besides, facilities of 24
Government laboratories (specialized labs/ other labs) are being utilized by BIS as and when
required.
Based on the lab recognition experience, Lab Recognition Scheme (LRS) document has
been revised and will replace existing LRS document after approval from the Executive
Committee.
Modernization and Up gradation of test facilities
Testing facilities for Flat Plate Solar Collector has been set up at Bengaluru lab with the
financial grant from Ministry of Non-renewable Energy Sources (MNES).
In the modernization programme, the Standing Committee had approved for modernization,
completion of partial test facilities, up gradation of test facilities, development of new test
facilities and infrastructure for BIS laboratories. Under this programme equipments to the
tune of around ` 4.80 crores have been purchased.
3
INFORMATION SERVICES
Technical Information Service Centre
Technical Information Services are provided to Industry, importers, exporters, individuals and
government agencies in response to their enquiries. In this endeavour, more than 350
enquiries were responded during the year 2011-12.
WTO/TBT Enquiry Point
BIS continues to handle the responsibilities of WTO-TBT Enquiry Point, as designated by
Ministry of Commerce. During the period TBT Notifications were disseminated and efforts
were made to sensitize the stakeholders
OTHER ACTIVITIES
(a) With a view to propagating the concept of standardization and quality systems
amongst small scale industries, industry awareness programmes are organized by
BIS. During the year, 14 such programmes were organized. BIS is creating
awareness among consumers about its activities by conducting consumer
awareness programmes through its network of regional and branch offices and by
participation in seminars/conferences organized by consumer organizations.
During the year, 135 such programmes were organized. In addition, 4 programmes
for Educational Utilization of Standards were also organized to propagate the
message of standardization and create awareness about latest Indian Standards in
various professional institutes and universities throughout the country.
World Standards Day 2011 was celebrated on 14th October 2011 on the theme
“International Standards- Creating Confidence Globally” to commemorate the
establishment of International Organization for Standardization (ISO). To mark this
occasion, seminars, exhibitions, lectures, meetings and open house programmes
were organized at Headquarters and Regional/Branch/Inspection Offices of BIS.
(b) Hindi Pakhwara was celebrated during 14-28 September 2011 wherein various
competitions in Hindi were organized.
(c) To spread awareness of BIS activities, programmes covering various BIS functions
were telecast. In addition programmes on BIS activities were also broadcast from
various kendras of AIR.
(d) Hosting of ISO General Assembly 2011- BIS hosted the 34th General Assembly
of International Organization for Standardization (ISO) during 19-24 Sep 2011 in
Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. 368 delegates from 127 countries and international
organizations participated in the General Assembly. During the General Assembly
week, 45th Plenary of ISO DEVCO was also organized.
4
(e) During the year, BIS participated actively in ISO/IEC Policy meetings and the ISO
Committee meetings on Developing Country matters (DEVCO). BIS also continued
to participate in ISO Committees / Subcommittees where India is a ‘P’ member and
where India holds Secretariat responsibilities.
(f) As per the directives of Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), Vigilance Awareness
Week was observed from 31 October – 5 November 2011 during which various
programmes throughout the country by all Regional and Branch Offices of the
Bureau were organized.
(g) The content of BIS website has been enriched and redesigned based on updated
inputs.
(h) Under the Eleventh Plan Schemes using Central Assistance, awareness among
consumers was generated regarding Gold Hallmarking through electronic media,
for the first time. In order to promote BIS participation at International level, BIS
Technical Committee Members were financed for attending ISO and IEC Technical
Committee meetings. Assistance was also provided for R&D Projects.
Infrastructure at NITS and 6 ROs/BOs has been upgraded and number of training
programmes were organized in identified areas.
(i) 44th International Training Programme on Standardization and Quality Assurance
for developing countries, 8th International Training Programme on Management
Systems for developing countries and 2nd International Training Programme on
Laboratory Quality Management were held during2011-12.
HUMAN RESOURCES
As on 31 March 2012, a total of 1578 persons were on roll in BIS .
INCOME AND EXPENDITURE
For the Twenty Third consecutive year i.e. 2011-12, Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
continued to be self reliant in meeting its expenditure and other liabilities. Total income
(excluding income from investment) during the year 2011-12 was Rs.25266.26 lakh against
Rs.22624.16 lakhs in the previous year resulting in an increase of 11.68%. The largest
contribution to the income was from ISI Certification Marking Fee which stood at
Rs.22393.16 lakh against Rs. 20012.25 lakh in the previous year i.e. an increase of
11.90%. The total revenue expenditure during the year 2011-12 stood at Rs.16970.32 lakh
as against Rs. 15401.71 lakh during 2010-11 registering an increase of 10.18%.
5
